title: Bridge: preserve OpenAI streaming / function-call semantics while enforcing Redwood structured-output
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Implement a compatibility layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/stream semantics) requests and responses and maps them to Redwood's internal streaming/event model while preserving function/tool-calling signals and enforcing Redwood structured-output validation. This ticket covers protocol translation, incremental streaming frame mapping, idempotency/backpressure handling, and a small runtime shim that runs in the gateway path for hosted and dedicated flows.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI-style streaming requests arrive to Redwood gateway and are translated to Redwood streaming events with 1:1 order preservation for user-assistant delta tokens

Function call invocation tokens ("function_call": name/arguments) are emitted as distinct structured events so internal tool router can intercept before final assistant finish; the original OpenAI stream structure (partial content + finish_reason) is reconstructible
Structured output schemas specified via Redwood schema hints are validated progressively; schema violations produce instrumented warnings and an optional final enforcement/rewrite step
Backpressure/hedging: gateway respects downstream backpressure and can translate OpenAI client cancellations into safe kv-cache invalidation and idempotent retry tokens

End-to-end test harness reproduces a minimal OpenAI streaming client (SSE/chunked) and verifies parity for 10 representative flows including function call, tool signals, JSON schema output, and truncated finishes
implementation_notes: Introduce a small translator module (oa_stream_adapter) that lives in gateway/service edge and exposes a narrow interface: ingestOpenAIStream(stream) -> RedwoodEventStream
Maintain 'chunk provenance' metadata per token chunk (source_offset, oa_frame_id) to allow replay/reassembly for debugging without exposing internals to clients

When a partial function_call appears in stream frames, buffer until the assistant emits either a 'finish' with function_call or explicit 'tool' instruction; emit a 'fncall.start' event at first function_call token and 'fncall.args' events for argument deltas
To keep latency low, validate schema incrementally using a fast streaming JSON parser with a configurable early-fail threshold; heavy validation runs async on finalization
Expose a telemetry tag 'compat.oa_stream=v1' and ID mapping between oa_request_id and redwood_request_id to ease debug traces across systems

Design trade-off: we will not attempt to transform OpenAI's ad-hoc 'role'-only delta edits into Redwood's richer structured assistant messages; instead we preserve raw deltas and attach structured interpretations when possible
test_plan: Unit tests for oa_stream_adapter: frame->event mapping, chunk provenance, fncall boundary detection
Integration test harness in CI that spins up gateway + mock-llm and runs SSE client verifying stream order, fncall events, and final content equivalence
Fuzz tests for truncated frames and out-of-order frame replay to ensure adapter idempotency
Load test: 1k concurrent streaming sessions with 75th/95th latency targets measured against current gateway baseline
Manual QA playbook: 10 sample prompts (including multi-tool chains and nested JSON outputs) with video capture of client streams and a checklist for schema enforcement behavior
